variants.description: p=1 heavy_hex ZNE with 5 layouts (vs 3 baseline)
variants.hypothesis: 5 layouts improves ZNE gain over 3 layouts on heavy-hex p=1. More CES diversity → better linear fit → higher gain.
variants.expected_outcome: Marginal improvement expected — 3 layouts already gives R²=0.998. If gain increases significantly → recommend 5 layouts on hardware. If no improvement → 3 layouts is sufficient (saves QPU time).

variants.description: p=1 heavy_hex ZNE with 32768 shots (vs 16384 baseline)
variants.hypothesis: 32768 shots improves ZNE gain over 16384 on heavy-hex p=1. Less shot noise → more accurate energy estimates → better ZNE.
variants.expected_outcome: Marginal improvement expected — 16384 already gives R²=0.998. If gain increases → recommend 32k shots on hardware. If no improvement → 16k is sufficient (halves QPU time).

variants.hypothesis: p=1 heavy_hex at h_test=2.625 still passes (ΔE/gap < 5%). This is closer to the valid regime boundary (h≥2.5) than our safe point (3.25), testing deployment flexibility.
variants.expected_outcome: PASS expected — h=2.625 is just above the estimated boundary h≥2.5. If PASS → hardware can test at h=2.625 (closer to phase transition). If FAIL → stick with h_test≥3.0 on hardware.

variants.description: p=1 heavy_hex with 1 restart (minimum VQE cost)
variants.hypothesis: p=1 heavy_hex with 1 restart achieves ΔE/gap < 5%. Bipartite graph → single global minimum → 1 restart sufficient.
variants.expected_outcome: PASS expected — NL-A1 (p=2, 1 restart) passed with 0.007. p=1 has simpler landscape → should also pass with 1 restart. If PASS → hardware SPSA needs only 1 run (minimum cost).

variants.description: p=2 heavy_hex ZNE with 5 layouts (can more layouts rescue p=2?)
variants.hypothesis: 5 layouts does NOT rescue p=2 ZNE on heavy-hex (CX=36 > threshold). Confirms that the failure is fundamental, not statistical.
variants.expected_outcome: FAIL expected — chain_1d p=2 N=10 with 7 layouts still fails (R²=0.08). More layouts cannot fix non-perturbative noise regime. Definitively closes the 'more layouts' question for heavy-hex.
